// profiles: One entry per profile; the key is its name, and the order here is the order in the sidebar's switch. Copy this file to profiles.json and make it yours. Check it with: python3 mods/t3-context/profiles.py check

work.label: Work
work.// badge, color: The text and theme colour of the account chips; badge defaults to the label.
work.// machines: Machines (hc machine ls) that are this profile's alone. A machine in no profile is shared: its spaces go by folder.
work.// folders: On a shared machine: folders whose spaces are this profile's.
work.// projects: What this profile works on; the key is the project's name. Each has its own coordinator (an agent that starts and tracks its tasks), so one project's rules and reports never reach another's. jira: its Jira project keys. places: where it is, one per machine (no "machine": this computer); a space there shows under the project in the sidebar. coordinator.folder: the folder (in the app home, or absolute) whose CLAUDE.md is the coordinator's instructions and where it keeps board.json; best a folder of the project's home repo.
work.// agents: reviewer: the agent that reviews for this profile (its program); leave it out for no reviewer. hc starts it through the template whose command runs it (hc templates). machines: per machine of this profile ("local": this computer), the only agents that may start there; an agent is a program any profile names here or as its reviewer, Claude Code's own subagents count as claude, and a machine left out (a sandbox) starts any agent.
work.// accounts: provider -> its settings. A secret is {"env": "NAME"} (a variable of your login shell or ~/.profile) or {"command": [...]}, never the value.

accounts.// claude: null: Claude Code's default config dir (~/.claude).
